summary: This note is a partial biography of Lina Medina. It says she has never revealed who fathered her child or how she became pregnant, and that her father was arrested on suspicion of child sexual abuse but released for lack of evidence, so the biological father was never identified. It also covers her adult life: she worked as a secretary at the Lima clinic of Lozada, married Raúl Jurado, and lived in a poor Lima district as of 2002, when she refused a Reuters interview. Her son grew up healthy and died in 1979 at age 40.
one_line: Biographical note on Lina Medina covering her unexplained pregnancy, her work as a secretary in Lima, her marriage, and her refusal of a 2002 Reuters interview.
key_facts: Medina has never revealed the father of her child or the circumstances of her impregnation.
Escomel suggested that Medina might not actually know herself, as she "couldn't give precise responses".
Lina's father was arrested on suspicion of child sexual abuse but was released due to lack of evidence.
The biological father of Medina's child was never identified.
Medina's son grew up healthy and died in 1979 at the age of 40.
In young adulthood, Medina worked as a secretary in the Lima clinic of Lozada.
Her work at the Lima clinic of Lozada gave her an education and helped put her son through high school.
Medina married Raúl Jurado, who fathered her second son in 1972.
As of 2002, Medina and Raúl Jurado lived in a poor district of Lima known as "Chicago Chico".
In 2002 Medina refused an interview with Reuters, just as she had turned away many reporters in years past.
